title: Son Doong Tours: How to Choose and Book (2027-28)
description: Son Doong tours have one operator. Here are its price, the fitness tests, the season, the cancellation rules and the Phong Nha cave treks to book if it is full.
h1: Son Doong tours: what the expedition involves, what it costs and how to get a place
intro: Son Doong tours are sold by one licensed operator, Oxalis Adventure: a 6-day, 5-night expedition for groups of 10, January to August, and, as of November 2026, Oxalis says 2027 is fully booked; its tour page says both that 2028 is fully booked and that limited places remain. So the real choice is between waiting for a later season and booking a shorter Oxalis cave trek in the same national park. This guide sets out the price, the fitness tests and the cancellation rules, and compares the alternatives.
keyPoints: **One operator.** Oxalis Adventure runs every Son Doong Cave Expedition. It calls oxalisadventure.com the official and only website for Oxalis tour bookings, so check any agent's departure against an Oxalis booking code.
**Price as of 27 November 2026:** {{vnd:80000000}} per person, according to the Oxalis tour page. This covers fees, VAT, meals, camping, safety gear and transfers in Dong Hoi, but not flights.

**Sold out for 2027:** according to Oxalis, as of November 2026. For 2028 its tour page says both "fully booked" and "limited availability remaining", so ask Oxalis. Vietnam News reported in January 2026 that the cave takes 1,000 visitors a year.
**Strict entry rules:** you must be 18-70, have done an overnight trek with at least 1,000 m of total climbing in the past 12 months, and be able to run 5 km in under 45 minutes.

**Cancellation is expensive:** more than 90 days out you lose a {{vnd:7000000}} processing fee. From 90 to 45 days out you lose half the price, and under 45 days you get no refund. Participants cannot be swapped.

blocks.text: **Oxalis Adventure (Oxalis Company Limited) is the only company running Son Doong tours.** It has operated them since the expedition officially launched in 2014. [Vietnam News](https://vietnamnews.vn/life-style/1763572/son-doong-cave-expedition-tour-fully-booked-until-2027.html) calls Oxalis the only company licensed to operate the tours in Vietnam. Oxalis says the provincial authorities approved the expedition in 2013 and pilot tours ran in August that year.

Son Doong is a cave nearly 9 km long, with a volume of 38.5 million cubic metres. It lies in the core zone of Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park, in Thuong Trach commune, Quang Tri province. Before the 2025 province mergers that area was Quang Binh province. According to [Oxalis's cave page](https://oxalisadventure.com/cave/son-doong-cave/), a local man, Ho Khanh, found the entrance in 1990, and a British-Vietnamese team led by Howard Limbert surveyed it in 2009-2010.

blocks.title: Agents and look-alike listings
blocks.text: Travel agencies and websites also advertise Son Doong tours. Oxalis describes [oxalisadventure.com](https://oxalisadventure.com/) as the official and only website for Oxalis tour bookings. If you book through an agent, ask which Oxalis departure date it holds, and get the Oxalis booking code before you pay.

sections.title: What does the Son Doong expedition involve?

blocks.text: The expedition involves about 28 km of jungle trekking, about 9 km inside the cave, roughly 50 river crossings and two nights camping in the cave. Oxalis lists it as 6 days, 5 nights at its "Challenging" grade, the hardest it offers. According to the [Oxalis tour page](https://oxalisadventure.com/tour/son-doong-cave-expedition-4d3n/), as of November 2026, the trip runs from January to August and stops in September because of the weather.

blocks.caption: Son Doong Cave Expedition, day by day (Oxalis Adventure tour page, read 27 November 2026)
rows: Arrive in Dong Hoi by 3pm, cave museum visit, compulsory safety briefing
About 14 km trek with around 30 knee-deep river crossings
Forest camp near the cave entrance
Descent into the main chamber, then on to the first doline (an open-roofed collapse in the cave)
Garden of Edam and the second doline
Underground lake, climb of the Great Wall (an 18 m ladder and about 72 m of steep rock), exit
Free morning, transfer back to Dong Hoi

blocks.text: A group of 10 guests goes with a cave expert, a tour guide, six safety assistants, two chefs and 18 porters. Porters carry up to 7 kg of your belongings. Anything you need while walking goes in your own 20-30 litre daypack. Tents are on raised platforms with mattresses and sleeping bags, and the cave camps have toilets and showers. Guides carry satellite phones, and Oxalis warns that medical help may take several hours to arrive.

sections.title: How much does a Son Doong tour cost?

blocks.text: A place on a shared (join-in) Son Doong expedition costs {{vnd:80000000}} per person, according to Oxalis Adventure, as of November 2026. Oxalis also quotes the price as US$3,000 per person. Its booking conditions say you pay by bank transfer in US dollars.

blocks.caption: What the Son Doong price includes (Oxalis tour page and booking conditions, read 27 November 2026)
rows: VAT, and the entrance and environmental service fee (stated as US$600)
Flights or travel to Dong Hoi
National park management and supervision fee (stated as US$20)
Pick-up and drop-off at Dong Hoi hotels, and transfers
Lodge, camping and farmstay nights; three meals a day
The insurance required by Vietnamese law, paying up to {{vnd:50000000}} per case

blocks.text: Oxalis lists a 10% discount for UOB cardholders and for returning Oxalis guests. A whole group of up to 10 can book a group departure. The booking conditions price this at US$30,000 per group, and private tours are priced on request. You can borrow trekking shoes in sizes 36-44 for a {{vnd:50000}} cleaning fee.

sections.title: How fit do you need to be for Son Doong?

blocks.text: You need to be fit enough to trek and climb for four days running, and Oxalis sets specific tests. If you give false or incomplete health details, Oxalis can cancel your booking without a refund. Guides can also send you back during the trip, and a guest turned back loses the whole price.

items: Age 18 to 70. Nobody under 18 joins any Son Doong expedition, and Oxalis takes no guest over 70 on any tour.
At least one overnight forest or mountain camping trek in the past 12 months, with at least 8 km a day and at least 1,000 m of total climbing.
An outdoor 5 km run in under 45 minutes.
Climbing five flights of stairs without stopping and without dizziness, chest pain or unusual breathlessness.

Oxalis says the trip is likely to be unsuitable if your blood pressure is above 140/80, or if you have diabetes, a heart condition or a musculoskeletal condition. You must send a health update 45 days before departure.

blocks.text: Which month is best for the trip?

Oxalis calls April and May the best time: the weather is mild, the landscape is green and there is mist inside the cave. January to March is cold, so you need a waterproof jacket and warm clothes for camp. June to August is the warmest period, when you can swim in the underground lakes. If you work at a school or language centre, check your leave against [the teaching year in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/the-teaching-year-in-vietnam) before you commit to a date.

sections.title: How do you book a Son Doong tour?

blocks.text: You book on Oxalis's own website: you choose a departure date, send a request with your health details, then pay within 24 hours of getting the invoice. As of November 2026, the Oxalis tour page says 2027 is fully booked; for 2028 it says both "fully booked" and "limited availability remaining". Its [availability calendar](https://oxalisadventure.com/check-availability/) does not mention a waiting list. To ask about later seasons, contact Oxalis through its website.

items.title: Check the requirements
items.text: Read the fitness and health conditions on the [Oxalis tour page](https://oxalisadventure.com/tour/son-doong-cave-expedition-4d3n/) before you choose a date.

items.title: Pick a date and send the request
items.text: Choose a departure in the booking calendar. Enter your health, medication, diet and trekking history accurately, and add any extras such as transfers. Oxalis emails you a booking code.

items.title: Talk to a consultant
items.text: Oxalis says a consultant contacts you within 48 working hours to confirm the details.

items.title: Pay on time
items.text: Pay by bank transfer within 24 hours of receiving the invoice and payment link, or the request may be cancelled automatically.

items.title: Buy insurance and prepare
items.text: Buy travel insurance that covers medical treatment, evacuation, guided caving and cancellation less than 90 days before departure. Then send your health update 45 days before you leave.

sections.title: Can you cancel or change a Son Doong booking?

blocks.text: You can cancel or change a Son Doong booking, but the earlier you do it, the more money you get back. Inside 45 days you get nothing back. You cannot pass your place to someone else: according to the [Oxalis booking conditions](https://oxalisadventure.com/about-us/booking-conditions/), the Son Doong expedition does not allow any change of participant.

blocks.caption: Refunds on a join-in Son Doong booking (Oxalis booking conditions, read 27 November 2026)
rows: {{vnd:7000000}} processing fee per person, the rest refunded
No fee (you pay any price difference), if places are free

blocks.text: If Oxalis cancels because of force majeure, it refunds the full tour price but not your flights or hotels. Refunds go back to the original card or account. Oxalis says domestic refunds take about 10-15 working days and international refunds 20-30.

sections.title: What can you book if Son Doong is full?

blocks.text: The closest alternative is Oxalis's Hang En Cave Adventure. It follows the first part of the Son Doong route and camps inside Hang En, the cave the Rao Thuong river flows through before it reaches the Son Doong system. On its Son Doong page, Oxalis itself suggests Hang Ba or Tu Lan for people who cannot get a place.

blocks.caption: Oxalis caving treks compared (Oxalis tour pages, prices per person, read 27 November 2026)

blocks.text: Hang En has the easiest fitness test of the four. You need one overnight trek, or one or two day treks, of at least 6 km a day with at least 500 m of total climbing in the past 12 months, plus the same run and stair tests. Hang Ba and Tu Lan use the same test as Son Doong, so they are also a good way to find out whether you could manage Son Doong later.
Look out for event and attraction tickets in Vietnam in eno.vn's [tickets and travel](/c/tickets-travel) category. The Son Doong expedition itself is booked only through Oxalis.

sections.title: What this guide does not cover

items: Flights and other ways to get to Dong Hoi: check them with the airline or transport company.
Which travel insurance covers guided caving: ask the insurer, and make sure the policy covers cancellation less than 90 days before departure.
Whether a medical condition rules you out: ask your doctor first, then Oxalis.
Day trips to Phong Nha's show caves: these are run separately from the Oxalis expeditions compared here.

faqs.q: How much does a Son Doong tour cost?
faqs.a: Oxalis Adventure prices the Son Doong Cave Expedition at US$3,000 per person, as of November 2026. That price includes VAT, the entrance and environmental service fee, park fees, meals, camping, safety gear and transfers in Dong Hoi. Flights to Dong Hoi, personal spending and extras are not included. The price in Vietnamese currency is in the costs section above.

faqs.q: Is Son Doong cave fully booked?
faqs.a: For 2027, yes. As of November 2026, the Oxalis Adventure tour page says 2027 is fully booked; for 2028 it says both fully booked and limited availability remaining, so ask Oxalis. In January 2026 Vietnam News reported that the 2026 and 2027 seasons had sold out, with visitors capped at 1,000 a year. The Oxalis availability calendar does not mention a waiting list, so ask Oxalis directly about later seasons.

faqs.q: Who is allowed to run tours into Son Doong cave?
faqs.a: Oxalis Adventure (Oxalis Company Limited) is the only company running Son Doong cave tours, and Vietnam News describes it as the only company licensed to operate them in Vietnam. The expedition officially launched in 2014. Oxalis calls oxalisadventure.com the official and only website for Oxalis bookings, so check that any agent's departure has an Oxalis booking code.

faqs.q: How fit do you need to be to visit Son Doong?
faqs.a: Oxalis requires Son Doong guests to have done at least one overnight trek in the past 12 months, with at least 8 km a day and 1,000 m of total climbing. Guests must also be able to run 5 km outdoors in under 45 minutes and climb five flights of stairs without stopping. Oxalis can cancel without a refund if health details turn out to be false.

faqs.q: Can children go on the Son Doong expedition?
faqs.a: No. Oxalis Adventure accepts no one under 18 on the Son Doong Cave Expedition, and no guest over 70 on any of its tours. Families with teenagers can look at Oxalis's Hang En Cave Adventure or Tu Lan Cave Expedition, which both take guests aged 16 to 70. Both still have their own fitness tests.

faqs.q: What is the best time of year to do the Son Doong tour?
faqs.a: Son Doong expeditions run from January to August and stop in September because of the weather. Oxalis Adventure calls April and May the best time, with mild weather and mist inside the cave. January to March is cold. June to August is the warmest period, when guests can swim in the underground lakes.

faqs.q: Is there a cheaper alternative to the Son Doong tour?
faqs.a: The closest cheaper alternative is Oxalis Adventure's Hang En Cave Adventure. It is a moderate two-day, one-night trek that follows the first part of the Son Doong route and camps inside Hang En cave. It costs far less than Son Doong, takes guests from 16, and runs from December to mid-September. The comparison table above has the prices.

faqs.q: Can I get a refund if I cancel my Son Doong tour?
faqs.a: Only if you cancel early. Under the Oxalis booking conditions, cancelling a shared Son Doong booking more than 90 days before departure costs a fixed processing fee per person, and the rest is refunded. From 90 to 45 days out, half the price is kept, and under 45 days nothing is refunded. Son Doong places cannot be passed to another person.
